title: Crüger to Müller, 1 July 1622
author: Peter Crüger
date_note: Taken as new style, which Danzig had adopted by then. Crüger gives both dates in other letters; as old style it would be 11 July, still before Kepler's of 15 July.
date_to_check: Danzig is assumed from where Crüger lived. Is 1 July new style, or old style (11 July)?
source: Peter Crüger's letter to Philipp Müller of 1 July 1622, written at Danzig, on Kepler's physical astronomy in the *Epitome*, which he finds pleasing but obscure, and on the *Astronomia Danica* of Longomontanus, just published on Tychonic principles, which he expects to trust more. The original is in the Bibliothèque de l'Observatoire, Paris (B, 1, 9; 89, 9. E. 27). Printed in extracts in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 107–108.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Crüger finds Kepler's physical astronomy pleasing but obscure, accuses him of bending Tycho's observations to fit his harmonies and Copernicanism, and turns hopefully to Longomontanus's newly published *Astronomia Danica*.

notes.note: The corrections added to or taken from a planet's mean motion to give its true place. Kepler found them from areas swept out, by what is now his second law.
Kepler's name for a planet's swinging nearer to and farther from the sun, which he compared with the arms of a balance (*Epitome*, book IV).

notes.on: the book on the more recent phenomena of the world
notes.note: Tycho's *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis* (1588), on the comet of 1577.
